title.narrative: HIV and AIDS Prevention, Care and Support Programme

description.narrative:
Diocese of Moshi Rainbow Centre HIV and AIDS programme covers one municipality and 3 districts including Moshi Municipality, Moshi Rural, Rombo and Hai districts within Kilimanjaro region. The total population of the area covered is 1,539,321 of which, 670,000 people are the Catholics (National Bureau of statistics 2002).
Majority of the population live in the rural areas with agriculture being the main economic activity. Coffee, wheat and barley are grown as cash crops. Other handy crops such as maize, beans, potatoes and bananas as well as animal husbandry and poultry keeping at a micro level. A minority of the population live in urban settings in townships and in Moshi municipality. They meet their daily sustenance through formal trading activities and as employees in different sectors and departments.
National HIV prevalence rate among the sexually active population is reported to be 7.0 %, with females having a slightly higher rate (7.7 %) than males (6.3 %). It is estimated that 1.3 million people including adults and children are living with HIV or AIDS in the country (the second National Multi-Sectoral Strategic Framework on HIV and AIDS, 2008-2012). In Kilimanjaro region where the Diocesan programme is based, HIV prevalence rate is 7.3 % against the national 7% (national surveys). It is estimated that about 87,741 people are living with HIV in Kilimanjaro region (NACP 2004).
The drivers of the HIV pandemic in Kilimanjaro region are multiple. These are shaped by the sexual relations of the people which are related to social, cultural, economic and awareness factors. They include promiscuous behavior, intergenerational sex, concurrent sexual partners and lack of knowledge of HIV infection. Others are poverty and transactional sex (commercial sex work), gender stereotypes, gender inequality and harmful cultural practices and prejudices. Mobility that leads to separation between spouses for temporary sexual relationships is also another factor and very prevalent in Kilimanjaro region.
This additional funding will support initiatives aimed to respond to these challenges. Areas of programme focus will include capacity building, provision of IEC materials, formation of clubs and provision of health education through structured seminars and workshops. Implementation will carried out at the zonal hospitals and at Rainbow Centres main office by project staff, trained counsellors, zonal coordinators and community volunteers.
The primary target group are the people living with HIV and AIDS and affected Orphans and Vulnerable Children including the destitute and People living with HIV and or AIDS including children, youth, men and women. Secondary beneficiaries will include the general public: religious leaders, community leaders, health workers, teachers and community based organisations. Cumulatively, the programme expects to reach 20,000 people both directly and indirectly by March 2011
